title: Odile and the Lantern
premise: In the river town of Vellmuth, on the eve of a revolution, Ivo Eastwick works quietly in her father's print shop, cutting type and keeping her head down. When the army requisitions the town, its grain, and the master ledger bearing every citizen's name, Ivo discovers the ledger is being rewritten to erase the dead, the disappeared, and the dissenters. Risking everything, she secretly prints a true account of what the occupation did, hiding the pages in plain sight as a children's book illustrated with lantern plates. As the river ice begins to thaw and the victors' historians arrive to seal the official record, Ivo must distribute her forbidden book before the presses are seized, ending with the truth drifting downstream on the first spring barges while she watches from the crowd, anonymous and finally unafraid.
about_author: Yara Reyes is a former bookbinder who spent a decade restoring damaged nineteenth-century ledgers and parish registers, an experience that taught her how easily records can be lost, altered, or quietly destroyed. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people who keep accounts — of grain, of names, of grief — and she lives near a river that freezes every winter.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Introduces the print shop, her father's failing eyesight, and her skill at cutting type no one notices. She sorts the town ledger for a customer and notes how names are the town's true currency. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking a longing to matter.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The army arrives, requisitions grain, billets officers, and seizes the master ledger as 'administrative material.' Ivo watches Captain Aldous Vane sign for it with a flourish. Emotional beat: the shock of ordinary life becoming collateral.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Copying a receipt, she glimpses the requisitioned ledger and sees entries already altered — a dead man marked as a debtor, a vanished family struck out. Emotional beat: the first cold understanding that records can lie.

chapters.title: The Lantern Maker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She visits Maren, a lantern-maker who lost her son to the occupation, and helps repair the lanterns hung for the winter festival. Their friendship forms around shared silence. Emotional beat: grief finding company without words.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Nails
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ordered to print occupation proclamations, she complies but begins keeping a private account of requisitions, arrests, and prices in her own hand. Emotional beat: the dangerous thrill of writing what is true.

chapters.title: Captain Vane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Vane visits the shop, courteous and chilling, commissioning a commemorative broadsheet praising the army's generosity. He compliments her type work and implies he knows she reads more than she should. Emotional beat: fear wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: A Name Struck Out
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Maren's son is officially recorded as a deserter who never existed; his mother's compensation claim is void. Ivo realizes the ledger doesn't just record the town — it is being used to unmake it. Emotional beat: rage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Plan in the Type Case
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She resolves to print the truth disguised as a children's book of lantern rhymes, each plate hiding a true account of the occupation. Her father, half-blind, offers the old press in the cellar. Emotional beat: hope that feels like treason.

chapters.title: Paper Is Scarce
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Procuring paper means bartering with a smuggler, Tomas, who asks no questions but wants payment in printed forgeries of travel passes. Ivo must decide how far complicity extends. Emotional beat: the corrupting arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The First Page
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She sets and prints the opening spread — a lantern rhyme concealing the names and dates of the disappeared. Her father inks the press with shaking hands. Emotional beat: terror and exaltation in equal measure.

chapters.title: A Search of the Shop
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Vane's men search the print shop after a proclamation is defaced. The hidden book passes inspection as a harmless primer, but Ivo's father is struck for 'surliness.' Emotional beat: the cost of being spared.

chapters.title: Maren Reads It Aloud
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. She shows Maren the book; Maren finds her son's true name and date of death hidden in a rhyme, and weeps. She offers the lantern workshop as a distribution point. Emotional beat: one grief answered becomes a network.

chapters.title: The Historians Are Coming
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Word arrives that the victors' commission of historians will arrive when the ice breaks, to compile the official record from the requisitioned ledger. The thaw becomes a deadline. Emotional beat: time suddenly audible, dripping.

chapters.title: Tomas's Price
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tomas demands more passes and then information about the book's contents, hinting he could sell her to Vane. Ivo weighs betrayal against exposure. Emotional beat: trust as a debt with compounding interest.

chapters.title: What Her Father Kept
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Her father reveals he once printed a suppressed pamphlet decades ago and lost a brother to the same rewriting of records; he gives her the hidden original type of his old press. Emotional beat: inheritance of a secret courage.

chapters.title: Ice Cracking at Night
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The river groans and shifts; the town gathers at the banks as the thaw begins. Vane posts guards on the print shops and announces the commission's arrival date. Emotional beat: dread and release braided together.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tomas, cornered by Vane's men, trades information. Soldiers raid the lantern workshop; Maren is arrested, and copies of the book are seized — but not all of them. Emotional beat: guilt, fury, and the arithmetic of what remains.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Working through the night with her father, she prints the final pages: the full true account, including Maren's arrest and Vane's signature on every altered entry. The press cracks under the strain. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the tool, and of safety.

chapters.title: Before the Commission
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The historians arrive; Vane presents the ledger as settled truth. Ivo, disguised as a shop assistant delivering printed primers, slips copies into the commission's own document crates. Emotional beat: audacity at the edge of collapse.

chapters.title: The River Opens
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Maren is released for lack of evidence as the seized 'children's book' circulates among the commission's clerks, who begin asking questions. The ice breaks fully; the first barges load. Emotional beat: the record slipping loose from its keepers.

chapters.title: What the Victors Read
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A junior historian reads a lantern rhyme aloud and finds the names beneath; the official record stalls as copies spread through the town and downstream. Vane searches for the printer and finds only type dust and a cracked press. Emotional beat: vindication arriving quietly, without a name attached.

chapters.title: Odile and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, coda. Spring settles; the ledger is reopened and amended, Maren's son restored to the record. Ivo prints a new edition of the book under its true title and hangs a lantern in the shop window. Emotional beat: belonging found not in safety, but in having been counted.
